A1.justification: Both complete 41-page PDFs describe TiC-LM and include Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the research content matches, with only minor first-page presentation differences.

before.justification: Section 6, Tables 2–3, and Appendix D report original continual-pretraining experiments with 3B-parameter models, including perplexity and downstream task results.

after.justification: Section 6, Tables 2–3, and Appendix D retain the original experimental results comparing continual-pretraining methods with periodically retrained Oracle models.

M1.justification: The data-construction procedures, model architecture, optimization schedules, replay strategies, and regularization methods remain identical, including the appendix algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Common Crawl, Wikipedia, StackExchange, and code-documentation coverage, together with the same 22 static downstream tasks. Appendix coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including Cyclic Cosine, AR schedules, Cyclic Rsqrt, Schedule-Free, replay variants, LwF, EWC, and the Oracle series.

E3.justification: Both retain the same 220B/440B token budgets, chronological training setup, tuning protocol, evaluation checkpoints, and metrics. Sections 4–6 and Appendices A–C contain no revised settings.

E4.justification: The decontamination check in Appendix A, dataset analyses in Appendix B, hyperparameter studies in Appendix C, and extended replay exploration in Appendix D.7 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 and 9 retain the same standard-deviation reporting based on three Cyclic Cosine runs and the same uncertainty-based highlighting conventions. No statistical reporting is added or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, plotted trends, and qualitative findings match throughout both PDFs, including Tables 2–3 and all extended results in Appendix D.

T1.justification: The perplexity definitions, replay-allocation formulas, regret formulation, and transfer-metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the same benchmark contribution and claims about matching retraining with 2.6 times less computation on general web data and domain-dependent replay tradeoffs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of forgetting, temporal alignment, and domain-dependent replay remain identical. The limitations concerning Oracle performance gaps, training-source coverage, fixed tokenization, and perplexity-based dynamic evaluations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain identical preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time estimates, and evaluation details. The code-access information and link destination are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and Appendix E contain the same cited works and research positioning, including the relationships to TiC-CLIP and earlier temporal language-model benchmarks.

P1.justification: The introduction adds a paragraph break before 'Taking inspiration from TiC-CLIP'. The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 2 April 2025 to v2 dated 8 May 2025; the paper's wording and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added paragraph break produces slight spacing and indentation changes in the first-page right column. Figures and tables are unchanged, and rendered pages 2–41 match exactly.

improvement.justification: The updated arXiv stamp and small first-page paragraph adjustment do not materially affect paper quality. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.
